parts.text: A student is investigating moments using a balancing method. Fig. 1.1 shows the apparatus. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student places the metre rule, without the loads, on the pivot and adjusts its position so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced. She keeps the rule at this position on the pivot throughout the experiment. Explain briefly why this position on the pivot may not be exactly at the 50.0 cm mark of the rule. ................................................................................................................................................... ............................................................................................................................................. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text: centre of mass/gravity not in centre (however expressed)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) She places a load P on the metre rule so that the edge that is furthest from the pivot is exactly at the 10.0 cm mark on the rule. She measures the distance a between this edge of the load P and the pivot, as shown in Fig. 1.1. She places a load Q on the metre rule and adjusts the position of load Q so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced. She measures the distance b between the centre of load Q and the pivot, as shown in Fig. 1.1. She repeats the procedure, with the edge of the load P that is furthest from the pivot at the 15.0 cm, 20.0 cm, 25.0 cm and 30.0 cm marks. All the readings are shown in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 a / cm b / cm 38.0 44.5 33.0 38.5 28.0 33.6 23.0 27.2 18.0 22.0 Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against b / cm ( x -axis). Start both axes at the origin (0,0). [4]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
graph:
axes correctly labelled and right way round
suitable scales starting from (0,0)
all plots correct to less than ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ........................................................ [2]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
triangle method used and seen on graph
triangle at least half of distance between extreme plotted points i.e. ∆a ⩾ 10

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Determine the intercept C on the x -axis of the graph. This is the value of b when a = 0. C = ........................................................ [1]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text: intercept correct to ½ small square – if graph not extrapolated, use the ruler tool

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text: width 2.5(0) cm / 25 mm with correct unit

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text:
statement to match results
justification to match statement and include idea of within (or beyond) limits of experimental accuracy

ms.label: 1(g)
ms.text:
difficulty in achieving exact balance/keeping the pivot in the same position/locating the centre of load (Q)/load(s)
slipping/load obscuring readings on rule
